description: Curated, source-verified Courtside Archive MiLB game recaps. Player tokens use MiLB player IDs rendered by player.html.

paragraphs: Lake Elsinore defeated Rancho Cucamonga 6–3 behind [[542357|Diego Goris]]’s grand slam in the fifth inning. Goris went 3-for-5 with four RBIs, breaking open a scoreless game after [[543232|Bengie González]], [[575928|Corey Adamson]] and [[593775|Gabriel Quintana]] reached base.

[[607067|Colin Rea]] earned the win with six scoreless innings, allowing five hits and striking out five. Rancho Cucamonga’s [[596840|Robbie Garvey]] answered with a three-run homer in the seventh, but the Quakes could not draw even.
[[592669|Hunter Renfroe]] added a solo homer in the eighth for Lake Elsinore. [[641627|Trevor Gott]] worked a scoreless ninth for the save, securing the Storm’s 6–3 victory.

San Jose defeated Stockton 6–2 at Municipal Stadium as [[596255|Jose Reyes]] carried a shutout into the seventh inning. Reyes worked 6.2 innings, allowing five hits and two runs while holding the Ports to two singles through the first six frames.

[[505830|Angel Villalona]] went 3-for-4 with a double and three RBIs, driving in [[624507|Ryder Jones]] in the first before a two-run double in the seventh. [[624414|Christian Arroyo]] hit a two-run homer in the fifth, extending his hitting streak to eight games.
Stockton finally broke through in the seventh when [[622168|Yairo Muñoz]] doubled home two runs. San Jose’s early offense and Villalona’s three-RBI game held up in the 6–2 series-clinching win.

Rancho Cucamonga defeated San Jose 7–3 at Excite Ballpark behind [[669023|Jeter Downs]]’ first professional multi-homer game. Downs hit a two-run homer in the third, then led off the seventh with another blast, finishing with three RBIs.

[[570482|Downs]] entered the night batting .196 in his first California League stint but used the two-homer game to continue a five-game stretch with three homers and six RBIs. Wills Montgomerie set the tone in his first start of the season with 4.2 hitless innings.
Rancho Cucamonga won its second straight game over San Jose, 7–3. Downs’ power display supplied the defining swing sequence in a road victory that pushed the Quakes to 19–11.

Rancho Cucamonga held off Lake Elsinore 8–6 to open the series at The Diamond. [[666659|Sauryn Lao]] went 3-for-5, falling a double short of the cycle; his sixth-inning homer opened a three-run frame that extended the Quakes’ lead to 8–3.

[[678760|Eddys Leonard]] collected two hits and three RBIs, including a two-run single in the eighth. [[672858|Edwin Mateo]] scored three times, while [[691949|Jake Vogel]] added two hits and drove in a run.

Lake Elsinore rallied for three runs in the eighth and brought the tying runs aboard, but Lao’s backhanded stop and throw to [[669797|Carlos Alejo]] covering first ended the inning. Alejo then recorded the final two outs in the ninth for the save.

Rancho Cucamonga broke open a close game with five runs in the fourth and rolled to an 8–2 win at Lake Elsinore. [[683425|Hyun-il Choi]] set the tone with five scoreless innings, allowing two hits and striking out three for the victory.

The Quakes made their fourth-inning push count: [[691949|Jake Vogel]] singled home a run, [[682942|Alex De Jesus]] followed with an RBI single, and [[678391|Jorbit Vivas]] lined a two-run double. Vogel added another RBI single in the ninth, while [[666659|Sauryn Lao]] and [[681955|Sam McWilliams]] each posted three hits.
Lake Elsinore’s only scoring came on [[673062|Jarryd Dale]]’s sixth-inning solo homer. [[672755|Aldry Acosta]] recorded seven outs without allowing a run to bridge the game into the late innings.

Lake Elsinore rallied from a three-run deficit in the ninth, then walked off Rancho Cucamonga 7–6 in 10 innings. [[672953|Gilberto Vizcarra]] delivered the game-ending single with one out in the bottom of the 10th, scoring [[678218|Brandon Valenzuela]].

Rancho Cucamonga had taken a 6–3 lead when [[680884|Aldrich De Jongh]] crushed a two-run homer in the eighth—his second blast of the night. De Jongh finished 4-for-5 with two homers and three RBIs; [[678760|Eddys Leonard]] doubled in a run and [[686781|Brandon Lewis]] had two hits and an RBI.

The Storm answered with three in the ninth, tying it on [[690987|Robert Hassell III]]’s sacrifice fly after [[665983|Kelvin Alarcon]]’s RBI single. Alarcon then worked a scoreless 10th and earned the win before Vizcarra’s final swing completed the comeback.

Rancho Cucamonga’s pitching staff combined on an 8-hit shutout in a 2–0 win at Lake Elsinore. [[679922|Carlos Duran]] worked four scoreless innings with five strikeouts, then [[672666|Adolfo Ramirez]] earned the win with 2 2/3 clean frames.

[[678391|Jorbit Vivas]] broke the scoreless tie in the fourth with an RBI single that brought home [[676356|Jonny DeLuca]]. DeLuca supplied the insurance run in the sixth, tripling to score [[686781|Brandon Lewis]].

The bullpen protected the slim lead throughout: [[673448|Nelfri Contreras]] threw a scoreless eighth and [[684195|Cameron Gibbens]] got the final four outs for the save. Duran, Vivas and DeLuca supplied the decisive work in a tight series win.

Rancho Cucamonga answered Lake Elsinore’s comeback attempt with a 9–3 win at The Diamond. [[666659|Sauryn Lao]] went 2-for-3 with a double, two walks, two runs and an RBI to lead a balanced Quakes lineup.

The Quakes scored three in the first, then broke it open with four in the fifth. [[678391|Jorbit Vivas]] collected two hits and two RBIs; [[678760|Eddys Leonard]] drove in two; and [[682942|Alex De Jesus]] doubled home a run in the fifth.

Lake Elsinore tied the game at 3 in the third, but did not score again. [[681147|Jake Cantleberry]] entered after the early rally and struck out four over 2 2/3 scoreless innings for the win, while [[669796|Jose E. Hernandez]] and [[674221|Franklin De La Paz]] finished the final 3 1/3 without a run.

Lake Elsinore piled up 16 runs to finish the series with a 16–8 win over Rancho Cucamonga. [[672355|Alison Quintero]] supplied the biggest swing, going 1-for-4 with a three-run homer, a sacrifice fly and four RBIs.

The Storm opened the game with a run, then surged ahead with five in the sixth and eight in the eighth. [[673062|Jarryd Dale]] tripled in a run during the sixth, and [[678218|Brandon Valenzuela]] followed with an RBI single before the eighth-inning barrage put the game away.

[[690987|Robert Hassell III]] tripled in a run, Valenzuela and [[672357|Jordy Barley]] added RBI doubles, and Quintero capped the eighth with his three-run homer. [[672353|Michell Miliano]] earned the win with two innings of one-run relief and five strikeouts.

Lake Elsinore erased a four-run ninth-inning deficit to stun San Jose 8–7 in the series opener. [[683494|Euribiel Angeles]] went 2-for-3 with two walks, two RBIs and three stolen bases, delivering the game-tying hit in the final rally.

The Storm’s early offense came from [[673062|Jarryd Dale]]’s two-run double, but San Jose answered with four runs in the sixth to build a 7–2 lead. [[665648|Ricardo Genovés]] homered for the Giants, while [[682266|Brett Auerbach]] went 4-for-5 with two RBIs.

Lake Elsinore began its ninth-inning charge with [[669090|Jack Stronach]]’s RBI double, then got an RBI single from [[678218|Brandon Valenzuela]] before Angeles brought home two. [[673309|Jose Garcia]] earned the win with two scoreless innings of relief as the Storm completed the comeback.

Lake Elsinore beat San Jose 9–3 behind a late offensive surge and strong work from [[682503|Felix Minjarez]]. Minjarez earned the win after allowing one hit over 4 2/3 scoreless innings with four strikeouts.

[[690987|Robert Hassell III]] led the Storm offense with two hits and three RBIs. He drove in a run with a second-inning single, added a sacrifice fly in the seventh and capped his night with another RBI single in the eighth.

Lake Elsinore had taken an early 3–0 lead, then broke a 3–3 tie with six runs across the seventh and eighth. [[665983|Kelvin Alarcon]] supplied a three-RBI day, including a two-run single in the eighth, while [[672385|Gabe Morales]] threw three scoreless relief innings.
San Jose used a pair of homers to beat Lake Elsinore 8–2. [[682617|Marco Luciano]] went 3-for-4 with a double, a homer, three runs and two RBIs in the Giants’ victory.

Luciano’s first-inning RBI single gave San Jose an early lead, and his solo homer in the third extended it. [[687466|Harrison Freed]] broke the game open with a three-run homer in the sixth, scoring Luciano and [[672744|Alexander Canario]].

The Giants’ bullpen sealed the result: [[678371|Ivan Armstrong]] allowed one run over three innings for the win, while [[690597|Austin Reich]] worked two scoreless innings with four strikeouts. [[690987|Robert Hassell III]] recorded two hits for Lake Elsinore and drove in a ninth-inning run.

San Jose edged Lake Elsinore 1–0 in a pitchers’ duel, with [[685068|Carson Ragsdale]] delivering 5 2/3 scoreless innings. Ragsdale allowed two hits, struck out 12 and carried the Giants into the late innings.

The game stayed scoreless until the eighth, when [[682617|Marco Luciano]] lined an RBI double to bring home [[682266|Brett Auerbach]]. Luciano finished with two hits, while Auerbach reached base twice in the low-scoring win.

The Giants’ relief corps completed a four-hit shutout. [[678738|Juan Sanchez]] earned the win with 2 1/3 hitless innings and four strikeouts, then [[663883|Brooks Crawford]] struck out two in a perfect ninth for the save.
San Jose took a 3–1 win over Lake Elsinore behind another big game from [[682617|Marco Luciano]]. Luciano went 2-for-4 with a solo homer and scored the Giants’ first run.

Lake Elsinore briefly led after [[680883|Sean Guilbe]]’s second-inning solo homer, but Luciano answered with his own blast in the bottom half. The Giants gained the lead for good in the fifth, when [[682641|Luis Matos]] reached on a force play that brought home two runs after a Storm error.

[[670247|Ty Weber]] earned the win with two scoreless innings, and [[663627|Clay Helvey]] closed with two scoreless frames for the save. [[678218|Brandon Valenzuela]] and [[683494|Euribiel Angeles]] each had two hits in the Storm loss.

San Jose completed a 2–1 win over Lake Elsinore behind [[669192|Wil Jensen]]’s dominant start. Jensen allowed two hits over five scoreless innings and struck out 10, earning the decision in a tightly played finale.
The Giants scored both of their runs in the first. [[682617|Marco Luciano]] reached on an error that brought home a run, then [[682266|Brett Auerbach]] forced in the second with a ground ball.

Lake Elsinore’s pitchers kept the game close, as [[676903|Noel Vela]] gave up one earned run over five innings and [[682503|Felix Minjarez]] worked two hitless relief frames. [[663883|Brooks Crawford]] struck out the side in the ninth for the save after the Storm pushed across a late run.

Stockton opened its home series with a 6–1 win over Lake Elsinore behind [[687578|David Leal]]’s six scoreless innings. Leal allowed three hits, did not walk a batter and struck out five for the victory.

The Ports built their lead with offense throughout the middle innings. [[678577|Junior Perez]] hit a solo homer in the fifth, and [[671732|Lawrence Butler]] followed a inning later with a two-run shot after [[691188|Robert Puason]] reached base.

[[672013|T.J. Schofield-Sam]] added a two-run single in the sixth, while [[660818|Jose Rivas]] drove in Stockton’s first run. [[690987|Robert Hassell III]] spoiled the shutout with a solo homer in the ninth for Lake Elsinore.
Stockton rallied late for a 5–4 win over Lake Elsinore. [[691016|Tyler Soderstrom]] delivered the decisive blow with a two-run homer in the eighth, turning a one-run deficit into a Ports lead.

Lake Elsinore had scored three runs in the third and added another in the eighth on [[672357|Jordy Barley]]’s sacrifice fly. [[683494|Euribiel Angeles]] went 2-for-4 with two runs, an RBI and two stolen bases, while [[681579|Nick Thwaits]] allowed one run over six innings with six strikeouts.

Stockton answered Soderstrom’s homer with a two-run double from [[660818|Jose Rivas]] later in the eighth. [[681979|Daniel Martinez]] earned the win with 3 1/3 innings of relief, holding the Storm to one run.

Stockton won a 10-inning thriller, 5–4, over Lake Elsinore. [[671732|Lawrence Butler]] drew a bases-loaded walk in the bottom of the 10th to force home the winning run after he had already driven in a run with a sacrifice fly.

Lake Elsinore used a pair of extra-base hits from [[672953|Gilberto Vizcarra]] and [[672357|Jordy Barley]] to take the lead in the fifth. Barley then hit a two-run homer in the seventh and finished with three RBIs, but the Storm could not hold the advantage.

Stockton tied the game with three runs in the seventh, then the bullpen kept it even. [[664330|Jose Mora]] earned the win with two scoreless innings and four strikeouts; [[691016|Tyler Soderstrom]] homered and scored twice for the Ports.

Lake Elsinore built a five-run lead and held on for a 5–4 victory over Stockton. [[669090|Jack Stronach]] supplied the decisive swing in the third inning, drilling a two-run double that brought home [[683494|Euribiel Angeles]] and [[690987|Robert Hassell III]].

[[680883|Sean Guilbe]] went 3-for-5 with an RBI, while [[673062|Jarryd Dale]] also recorded three hits. Angeles collected two hits and scored once as the Storm scored in each of the first three innings to establish the cushion.

After Stockton rallied for three runs in the fifth, [[692020|Ruben Galindo]] completed four innings to earn the win. [[672353|Michell Miliano]] then struck out three in a scoreless ninth for the save, preserving the one-run result.
Lake Elsinore beat Stockton 6–2 behind [[676903|Noel Vela]]’s dominant start. Vela allowed one hit and one run across six innings, struck out 11 and earned the victory.

[[672357|Jordy Barley]] went 2-for-4 with a two-run homer in the third, scoring [[678222|Angel Solarte]] to give the Storm an early lead. Solarte and [[690987|Robert Hassell III]] each had two hits, while [[673062|Jarryd Dale]] collected two hits and two RBIs.

Stockton pulled even on a solo homer in the eighth, but Lake Elsinore answered with four in the ninth. A run scored on an error before Dale’s two-run single drove in Barley and Angeles, and the Storm bullpen finished the 6–2 win.

Lake Elsinore held off Stockton 9–7 to finish the series at Banner Island Ballpark. [[690987|Robert Hassell III]] went 3-for-5 with two doubles and two RBIs, driving in [[683494|Euribiel Angeles]] in both the second and sixth innings.

The Storm built a 7–1 lead in the first two innings. [[672357|Jordy Barley]] launched a two-run homer in the second, and [[669090|Jack Stronach]] followed with a two-run single; Angeles scored three times in a 3-for-5 day.

Stockton answered with four runs in the second and drew within two in the fifth, but Lake Elsinore added insurance in the sixth and seventh. [[678736|Miguel Rondon]] earned the win, and [[672353|Michell Miliano]] struck out four over 1.2 scoreless innings for the save.

Rancho Cucamonga overwhelmed Lake Elsinore 15–4 behind a historic night from [[678391|Jorbit Vivas]]. Vivas went 6-for-6 with a grand slam, four RBIs and three runs, tying a 24-year-old Quakes franchise record for hits in a game.

The Quakes broke the game open with 10 runs in the fifth inning, capped by Vivas’ grand slam. [[678760|Eddys Leonard]] hit a solo homer and finished with three hits and two RBIs, while [[681955|Sam McWilliams]] had three hits, scored three runs and drove in one.

Rancho Cucamonga totaled 22 hits in the rout. [[679922|Carlos Duran]] struck out seven over four innings, and [[669797|Carlos Alejo]] earned the win with a scoreless fifth; for Lake Elsinore, [[669101|Matthew Acosta]] homered and [[690987|Robert Hassell III]] drove in two runs.

Lake Elsinore defeated Rancho Cucamonga 8–5 behind [[678218|Brandon Valenzuela]]’s four-hit night. Valenzuela went 4-for-5 with a double, triple, two runs and four RBIs, falling a homer shy of the first cycle in Storm franchise history.

The Storm took control with three runs in the fourth, as [[673062|Jarryd Dale]] and [[680883|Sean Guilbe]] delivered RBI singles before [[678222|Angel Solarte]] was hit by a pitch with the bases loaded. Rancho answered with four runs in the fifth to pull even.

Valenzuela immediately put Lake Elsinore back ahead with a two-run single in the bottom of the fifth, then added another two-run single in the eighth. [[673325|Ramon Perez]] earned the win with 2.1 scoreless innings, and the Storm bullpen closed out the 8–5 result.

Rancho Cucamonga beat Lake Elsinore 7–4 after [[686781|Brandon Lewis]] broke open a tight game with a three-run homer in the eighth. Lewis’ fifth home run of the season scored [[678760|Eddys Leonard]] and [[681955|Sam McWilliams]], turning a one-run lead into a four-run cushion.

The Quakes struck first on McWilliams’ two-run homer in the opening inning, but Lake Elsinore answered with two runs of its own. [[690987|Robert Hassell III]] went 3-for-5 with a triple, two runs and two RBIs for the Storm, including RBI singles in the first and seventh.

[[672896|Wladimir Chalo]] added a two-run homer for Rancho Cucamonga in the fifth. [[674221|Franklin De La Paz]] earned the win with 2.2 scoreless innings of relief, while the Quakes’ late power held up for the 7–4 victory.

Rancho Cucamonga defeated Lake Elsinore 11–6 behind [[682616|Diego Cartaya]]’s four-RBI night. Cartaya went 2-for-3 with a homer, two walks and two runs, opening the scoring on a three-run blast in the second before adding an RBI single in the fifth.

[[666659|Sauryn Lao]] hit a three-run homer in the second, and [[678760|Eddys Leonard]] added a three-run night with a homer, a walk and an eighth-inning two-run shot. The Quakes took charge with five runs in the fifth and added another in the sixth.

[[683425|Hyun-il Choi]] earned the win with four scoreless innings and five strikeouts. Lake Elsinore’s [[687084|Joshua Mears]] posted two hits, including a homer, while [[672355|Alison Quintero]] went 2-for-4 with three RBIs in the loss.

Lake Elsinore rallied past Rancho Cucamonga 8–6 as [[690987|Robert Hassell III]] supplied four RBIs. Hassell went 2-for-4, hitting a three-run homer in the fifth that tied the game and adding an RBI single in the seventh to put the Storm ahead.

Rancho Cucamonga jumped in front on [[676356|Jonny DeLuca]]’s three-run homer in the first, while [[666659|Sauryn Lao]] homered in both the second and fourth. The Storm stayed close as [[687084|Joshua Mears]] hit a solo homer and [[683494|Euribiel Angeles]] went 3-for-5 with three runs.

Lake Elsinore moved ahead with three runs in the seventh and added an insurance run in the eighth. [[690425|Chase Walter]] earned the win with a scoreless inning, and [[678980|José Geraldo]] worked the final two innings for the save.

Lake Elsinore rallied past Rancho Cucamonga 8–5 to split the series. [[687084|Joshua Mears]] hit two homers and drove in three runs, including a two-run shot in the five-run seventh that put the Storm ahead for good.

Rancho Cucamonga opened a 2–0 lead in the first, and [[686781|Brandon Lewis]] added a solo homer in the third as part of a 4-for-5 day. The Storm stayed close on an RBI single from [[678218|Brandon Valenzuela]] and Mears’ solo homer in the fourth.

Lake Elsinore turned the game in the seventh, first scoring on Valenzuela’s sacrifice fly before Mears went deep with [[669090|Jack Stronach]] aboard. [[688195|Zack Mathis]] then hit a two-run homer, and [[673325|Ramon Perez]] struck out four over two scoreless innings for the save.

Lake Elsinore scored six late runs to beat Inland Empire 6–2 in San Bernardino. [[672357|Jordy Barley]] broke a 1–1 tie with a two-run homer in the eighth, scoring [[678222|Angel Solarte]] and putting the Storm in front.

Inland Empire had carried a lead behind [[677611|Jose Reyes]]’ solo homer in the third, while [[673820|Robinson Piña]] struck out nine across seven scoreless innings. Lake Elsinore stayed within reach and surged once the 66ers turned to the bullpen.

The Storm sealed the game with four runs in the ninth. [[672953|Gilberto Vizcarra]] lined a three-run single after an RBI hit-by-pitch, while [[673325|Ramon Perez]] earned the win with two innings of one-run relief.

Lake Elsinore defeated Inland Empire 6–2 behind [[683494|Euribiel Angeles]]’ two-hit, two-RBI game. Angeles drove in the Storm’s first run with a third-inning single, then added another RBI single in the ninth to help put the game away.

The Storm broke a 2–2 tie in the fifth when [[673062|Jarryd Dale]] reached on a throwing error that brought home two runs. [[678218|Brandon Valenzuela]] followed with a sacrifice fly, and Lake Elsinore carried a three-run advantage into the late innings.

[[687723|Levi Thomas]] earned the win with five innings of two-run ball. Lake Elsinore added two more runs in the ninth on hits from Angeles and Dale, securing the second straight 6–2 victory over the 66ers.
Inland Empire edged Lake Elsinore 4–3 behind [[669081|Jack Dashwood]]’s strong start. Dashwood allowed one run over 4.2 innings, struck out six and earned the win as the 66ers held on late.

[[669236|Jeremiah Jackson]] hit a two-run homer in the fourth, and [[677611|Jose Reyes]] added a solo homer in the fifth to give Inland Empire its margin. The 66ers’ pitching staff protected the lead after Lake Elsinore rallied.

The Storm scored twice in the fifth on [[683494|Euribiel Angeles]]’ triple and [[690987|Robert Hassell III]]’s RBI groundout, then drew within one when Hassell singled home [[672357|Jordy Barley]] in the seventh. Inland Empire closed out the 4–3 win.
